_about: Human verdicts on disagreements between the two Wikipedia surfaces.
When scripts/harvest_raga_articles.py finds that a raga's article and the
list page give different degree sequences, it records the disagreement on
both sources and resolves nothing - deliberately, per specs/05-data-accuracy.md.
This file is where a person resolves one, and it is separate from
data/ragas.json for one hard reason: ragas.json is regenerated by the
scraper, so a verdict written into it is destroyed by the next re-scrape.
Kept here, scripts/apply_article_harvest.py merges it back in every time.
verdict: 'stored-correct'  - data/ragas.json is right, the article is wrong
'article-correct' - the article is right; ragas.json needs fixing,
which is a scraper or source question, not an
edit to make here
'person-correct'  - neither surface is right. The reviewer's reading
supersedes both, and the correction carries it.
Added 2026-08-08 for Asaveri, whose reading
matched neither Wikipedia page: the other three
verdicts can only pick a side or decline to, so
recording it as 'article-correct' would have made
this file claim the article said something it
does not. Unlike the other verdicts it does not
need the two sources to disagree - a person may
correct a raga they agree on - so it is exempt
from the staleness check alongside
'article-correct', for a different reason.
by: who decided. 'person' means a human with the training to judge it -
the same standing the 'person' citation type carries in raga_details.json.
correction: optional. The raga as it should read, in the schema's own note
shape, applied by apply_article_harvest.py rather than typed into
ragas.json, which the scraper would overwrite. May carry arohana,
avarohana, name, aliases, id and variants. Give every direction the
reviewer confirmed, not only the one that changed - an unchanged
direction recorded here is what stops a later re-scrape from breaking it
too.
`variants` (added 2026-08-08) are readings kept *beside* the primary
rather than instead of it, each {direction, notes, source, set}. Asaveri
is the case: both Wikipedia surfaces give a defensible avarohana that
differs from the reviewer's and from each other, and discarding them
would hide the disagreement the review exists to record. The list
REPLACES any existing variants rather than appending, so a second run
cannot pile up duplicates, and each one goes through the sthayi octave
rule exactly as the primaries do.
NO SWARA NAMES IN PROSE. A note never spells a scale as text: swara labels
depend on the reader's numbering convention (CLAUDE.md, 'Notation
format'), so 'S G2 M1 P N2 S' typed into a sentence is right for one
reader and wrong for another, and it sat on screen contradicting the
very scale it was describing. Put the degrees in `scales` and reference
them from the note text as {name}; the page renders each one under
whatever convention the reader has chosen.

darbar.note: Darbar is {arohana} ascending and {avarohana} descending. The list page's avarohana was scraped as {scraped} - a leading Rishabha-Shadja pair that does not belong, and an interior Shadja read as the lower octave. No avarohana starts a step above its own Sa. The article's reading is the correct one and is what is applied here; the arohana was already right and is recorded unchanged so a re-scrape cannot break it either.

suddha-dhanyasi.note: The stored {stored} is the documented form and the case is settled. The article's infobox calls this raga's Gandhara and Nishada shuddha, which the mainstream pitch-order table reads as {article} - and that is simply wrong for this raga. Note also that the wrong reading would not even be the raga an earlier version of this note claimed: those degrees are Suddha Saveri, not Madhyamavati.

udayaraga.note: The same raga as Suddha Dhanyasi under another name, the same article wording, and the same verdict: the stored {stored} is correct and the article's shuddha Gandhara and Nishada are wrong. Renaming this entry to Udayaravichandrika, the title its own article carries, was tried on 2026-08-04 and reverted: data/ragas.json already holds a different raga of that name under mela 9, and the rename would have put two unrelated scales behind one name. It stays Udayaraga.

asaveri.note: Asaveri is {arohana} ascending and {avarohana} descending. Neither Wikipedia surface has it: the list page gives {scraped} and the article {article}, and those two differ from each other in one note only, which is why the raga carries a recorded disagreement at all. The reviewer's reading differs from both in three places - the interior Shadja is the upper one, the Madhyama-Panchama pair is the other way round, and the Rishabha before the Gandhara is not there. The first of those three the sthayi solver derives independently from the run's own shape, which is the part of this verdict that is not taken on trust. The arohana is unchanged from both surfaces and is recorded anyway so a re-scrape cannot break it. Both surfaces' avarohanas are kept as alternatives rather than discarded: each is defensible, and the page should show the disagreement instead of hiding it behind one chosen reading. Both are recorded with the interior Shadja as the upper one, which is the single correction they and the reviewer agree on. Keeping the article's alternative also gives the raga's declared anya swara - a Rishabha the reviewer's reading does not use - a note in the data that actually uses it.
